title: fissile audit output
description: `fissile audit --format json` (FS-004-check-audit.2): standing findings plus optional inventory sections. `top` appears with --top, `stale` and `loose` with --stale-exceptions, `coverage` with --rule-coverage, and `history` with --history.

findings.description: Standing findings, same shape as check output.

silenced.description: Overflows accepted by an exception, carried for attribution (FS-003-exceptions.5).

exceptions.description: Registry entry and distinct literal path-expression totals per kind across both registries (FS-004-check-audit.2). `structural` and `deferred` count entries; `structural_paths` and `deferred_paths` deduplicate identical path strings, with structural taking precedence. Glob expressions count once without expansion. Always present, including all-zero.

stale.description: Exceptions whose path matches no scanned file (audit --stale-exceptions). An entry is identified by the registry it lives in and the path it accepts, since the list spans both registries (DF-005-exception-identity).

loose.description: Exact-path exceptions whose ceiling stands more than one [exceptions.bump] step above the file they accept, or sits exactly on it (audit --stale-exceptions, FS-003-exceptions.7). Stale is the other half: an entry accepting a file that is gone.

severity.description: Which registry holds the entry, and therefore which of the rule's two limits it accepts.

limit.description: The rule limit at that severity — what the entry exists to accept, and the floor `retune_to` never drops below.

no_headroom.description: 1 when the ceiling equals the measurement, so the entry silences the finding today and stops on the next unrelated commit; 0 when it stands more than a bump step above the file (FS-003-exceptions.7).

retune_to.description: The ceiling `fissile exception retune` would write, never below the limit the entry accepts, and for an entry without headroom the step's next multiple strictly above the one recorded. Null where `retune` would refuse or write nothing (DF-010-stated-ceilings-are-exact.2); `stated_range` carries the remedy instead.

stated_range.description: The ceiling a stated `--max` should take when `retune_to` is null: `min` alone where the measured form would write the number already recorded, and `min` with `max_excluded` where a range keeps the ceiling under the hard limit. Null whenever `retune_to` holds a value — exactly one of the two is set, except where no ceiling under the hard limit grants headroom and there is none to name, where both are null.

min.description: The floor of the range, where `max_excluded` is present: the lowest ceiling that still silences the finding, and for an entry without headroom the lowest that grants any. Where `max_excluded` is absent, `min` is the value to state, as the enclosing description says.

max_excluded.description: The hard limit the ceiling has to stay under. Absent where `min` is the value to state rather than the floor of a range.

silences_nothing.description: 1 when the file no longer crosses that limit at all, so removing the entry is the remedy rather than lowering it.

history.description: Exception movement and continuous debt ages for the committed revision range requested by audit --history (FS-004-check-audit.2.1).
